work_accident.reformulated_text:
A process for gathering information about work accidents and almost work accidents involves the following steps and conditions. 

An accident is considered a work accident under insured gainful employment if it occurs in specific circumstances, including at a location, time, and with a cause that correlates to the insured employment, when working from home, on the direct route to or from work, during training sessions, or when visiting a doctor with prior notification to the employer. 

For kindergarten children, schoolchildren, and students, an accident is considered a work accident if it occurs in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the school or university education, during school events, on the direct route to or from school, or when performing practical tasks prescribed by the curriculum. 

In agricultural or forestry establishments, accidents can be considered work accidents even if they do not occur directly while performing the insured employment. 

Certain accidents outside of professional activity are also considered work accidents, including activities under unemployment/labour market support services, assisting with an accident, donating blood, or training as a member of a volunteer aid organisation. 

Employees must inform their employer immediately of any work accident, near accident, serious and immediate risk to safety and health, or defect in protection systems. 

The employer must report any work accident resulting in a fatality or serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate if it has not been reported to emergency services. 

Every work accident resulting in a fatality or injury that prevents a person from working for three days must be reported to the responsible accident insurance provider within five days. 

Self-employed individuals must report accidents involving themselves or their employees to the accident insurance provider in good time. 

Students and schoolchildren must report accidents to the competent directorate, and schools must report work accidents to the responsible accident insurance provider within five days. 

In cases of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately to avoid releasing the provider from their obligation to perform, and fatalities must be reported within three days even if the accident has already been reported. 

These conditions and reporting requirements apply to various cases and persist over time, with transitions from one condition to another caused by the occurrence of work accidents, near accidents, or changes in employment status.

job_application.reformulated_text: The process involves several entities: the job applicant, job applications, companies, and job offers. The job applicant is expected to regularly report the companies to which they have submitted job applications. Based on these reported job applications, new potential job offers are generated and sent to the job applicant. Companies are required to confirm receipt of job applications and provide a rating for the application. A job interview can be arranged through negotiation. If a company wishes to hire the job applicant, they enter a probation phase. After completing the probation phase, both the job applicant and the company can provide ratings for each other. However, the text does not specify what triggers the transition from the probation phase to the rating step, nor what the criteria are for a company to want to hire the job applicant. The text also does not specify what happens during the probation phase. Reviews of a company are only visible to job applicants after a period of 1 year, but the text does not specify whether this applies to all reviews or only those from job applicants who have completed the probation phase. If a job becomes permanent, the process ends for that job, unless the job applicant rated the company C or less, in which case they continue to receive new job offers, but are no longer required to report their job applications. The text does not specify what is meant by a job becoming permanent, nor what the implications are of receiving a rating of C or less.

work_accident.reformulated_text:
The process involves several entities: work accidents, insured individuals, employers, and accident insurance providers. A work accident is considered to occur in various circumstances, including when it happens in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the insured employment. The text does not specify whether these circumstances are exhaustive or if there are other situations that may also be considered work accidents.

For insured gainful employment, specific examples of work accidents are given, including accidents that occur while working from home, on the direct route to or from work, during training sessions, and while making use of advocacy groups or professional associations. The text does not specify whether these examples are mutually exclusive or if there can be overlap between them.

For kindergarten children, schoolchildren, and students, a work accident is considered to occur in situations such as when the accident happens in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the school or university education, or when taking part in a school event or school-related event. The text does not specify whether these situations are the only ones that are considered work accidents for these individuals.

In an agricultural or forestry establishment, accidents can be considered work accidents even if they do not occur directly while performing the insured employment. The text does not specify what constitutes "directly while performing the insured employment" or how this is determined.

Certain accidents are considered the same as work accidents outside of professional activity, including activities under unemployment/labour market support services and training or serving as a member of a volunteer aid organisation. The text does not specify whether these accidents are automatically considered work accidents or if there are additional criteria that must be met.

When a work accident occurs, the employee must inform the employer immediately. The employer must then report any work accident that leads to a fatality or serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate, if it has not been reported to the emergency services. The text does not specify what constitutes a "serious injury" or how this is determined.

In addition, every work accident in which a person with accident insurance has been killed or injured in such a way that they are unable to work for three days must be reported to the responsible accident insurance provider within five days. The text does not specify what happens if this reporting requirement is not met or if the accident is not reported within the specified timeframe.

For self-employed individuals, accidents involving people they employ and those that involve themselves must be reported to the accident insurance provider in good time. The text does not specify what constitutes "good time" or how this is determined.

Students and schoolchildren should report accidents to the competent directorate, while schools, educational facilities, and universities are obliged to report every work accident through which a person with accident insurance is physically injured or killed within a maximum of five days to the responsible accident insurance provider in triplicate. The text does not specify what happens if this reporting requirement is not met or if the accident is not reported within the specified timeframe.

In the case of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately in line with the conditions and to avoid the provider from being released from the obligation to perform. If there are fatalities, this must be reported within three days, even if the accident has already been reported. The text does not specify what constitutes "immediately" or how this is determined.
